PREFACE
This Code constitutes a complete recodification of the general and permanent ordinances of the City of Rossville, Georgia.
Source materials used in the preparation of the Code were the 1976 Code, as supplemented through December 11, 1995, and ordinances subsequently adopted by the mayor and council. The source of each section is included in the history note appearing in parentheses at the end thereof. The absence of such a note indicates that the section is new and was adopted for the first time with the adoption of the Code. By use of the comparative tables appearing in the back of this Code, the reader can locate any section of the 1976 Code, as supplemented, and any subsequent ordinance included herein.
The chapters of the Code have been conveniently arranged in alphabetical order, and the various sections within each chapter have been catchlined to facilitate usage. Notes which tie related sections of the Code together and which refer to relevant state law have been included. A table listing the state law citations and setting forth their location within the Code is included at the back of this Code.
Chapter and Section Numbering System
The chapter and section numbering system used in this Code is the same system used in many state and local government codes. Each section number consists of two parts separated by a dash. The figure before the dash refers to the chapter number, and the figure after the dash refers to the position of the section within the chapter. Thus, the second section of chapter 1 is numbered 1-2, and the first section of chapter 6 is 6-1. Under this system, each section is identified with its chapter, and at the same time new sections can be inserted in their proper place by using the decimal system for amendments. For example, if new material consisting of one section that would logically come between sections 6-1 and 6-2 is desired to be added, such new section would be numbered 6-1.5. New articles and new divisions may be included in the same way or, in the case of articles, may be placed at the end of the chapter embracing the subject, and, in the case of divisions, may be placed at the end of the article embracing the subject. The next successive number shall be assigned to the new article or division. New chapters may be included by using one of the reserved chapter numbers. Care should be taken that the alphabetical arrangement of chapters is maintained when including new chapters.
Page Numbering System
The page numbering system used in this Code is a prefix system. The letters to the left of the colon are an abbreviation which represents a certain portion of the volume. The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion. In the case of a chapter of the Code, the number to the left of the colon indicates the number of the chapter. In the case of an appendix to the Code, the letter immediately to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. The following are typical parts of codes of ordinances, which may or may not appear in this Code at this time, and their corresponding prefixes:
CHARTER | CHT:1
CHARTER COMPARATIVE TABLE | CHTCT:1
CODE | CD1:1
CODE APPENDIX | CDA:1
CODE COMPARATIVE TABLES | CCT:1
STATE LAW REFERENCE TABLE | SLT:1
CHARTER INDEX | CHTi:1
CODE INDEX | CDi:1
Indexes
The indexes have been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been placed under several headings, some of which are couched in lay phraseology, others in legal terminology, and still others in language generally used by local government officials and employees. There are numerous cross references within the indexes themselves which stand as guideposts to direct the user to the particular item in which the user is interested.
Looseleaf Supplements
A special feature of this publication is the looseleaf system of binding and supplemental servicing of the publication. With this system, the publication will be kept up-to-date. Subsequent amendatory legislation will be properly edited, and the affected page or pages will be reprinted. These new pages will be distributed to holders of copies of the publication, with instructions for the manner of inserting the new pages and deleting the obsolete pages.
Keeping this publication up-to-date at all times will depend largely upon the holder of the publication. As revised pages are received, it will then become the responsibility of the holder to have the amendments inserted according to the attached instructions. It is strongly recommended by the publisher that all such amendments be inserted immediately upon receipt to avoid misplacing them and, in addition, that all deleted pages be saved and filed for historical reference purposes.
Acknowledgments
This publication was under the direct supervision of Ronald McLaughlin, Supervising Editor, of the Municipal Code Corporation, Tallahassee, Florida. Credit is gratefully given to the other members of the publisher's staff for their sincere interest and able assistance throughout the project.
The publisher is most grateful to W. L. North, Mayor, John Davis, City Attorney, and Bobbie Alexander, City Clerk, for their cooperation and assistance during the progress of the work on this publication. It is hoped that their efforts and those of the publisher have resulted in a Code of Ordinances which will make the active law of the city readily accessible to all citizens and which will be a valuable tool in the day-to-day administration of the city's affairs.

All editorial enhancements of this Code are copyrighted by Municipal Code Corporation and the City of Rossville, Georgia. Editorial enhancements include, but are not limited to: organization; table of contents; section catchlines; prechapter section analyses; editor's notes; cross references; state law references; numbering system; code comparative table; state law reference table; and index. Such material may not be used or reproduced for commercial purposes without the express written consent of Municipal Code Corporation and the City of Rossville, Georgia.

ADOPTING ORDINANCE
ORDINANCE NO. 354
An Ordinance Adopting and Enacting a New Code for the City of Rossville, Georgia; Providing for the Repeal of Certain Ordinances Not Included Therein; Providing a Penalty for the Violation Thereof; Providing for the Manner of Amending Such Code; and Providing When Such Code and This Ordinance Shall Become Effective.
Be it Ordained by the Mayor and Council of Rossville, GA:
Section 1. The Code entitled ``The Code of Ordinances of the City of Rossville, Georgia, published by Municipal Code Corporation, consisting of Chapters 1 through 78, each inclusive, is adopted.
Section 2. All ordinances of a general and permanent nature enacted on or before April 14, 1997, and not included in the Code or recognized and continued in force by reference therein, are repealed.
Section 3. The repeal provided for in Section 2 hereof shall not be construed to revive any ordinance or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent ordinance that is repealed by this ordinance.
Section 4. Unless another penalty is expressly provided, every person convicted of a violation of any provision of the Code or any ordinance, rule or regulation adopted or issued in pursuance thereof shall be punished by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, or imprisonment not to exceed 30 days, or by both such fine and imprisonment. Each act of violation and each day upon which any such violation shall occur shall constitute a separate offense. The penalty provided by this section, unless another penalty is expressly provided, shall apply to the amendment of any Code section whether or not such penalty is reenacted in the amendatory ordinance. In addition to the penalty prescribed above, the city council may pursue other remedies such as abatement of nuisances, injunctive relief and revocation of licenses or permits.
Section 5. Additions and amendments to the Code when passed in the form as to indicate the intention of the mayor and council to make the same a part of the Code shall be deemed to be incorporated in the Code, so that reference to the Code includes the additions and amendments.
Section 6. Ordinances adopted after April 14, 1997, that amend or refer to ordinances that have been codified in the Code shall be construed as if they amend or refer to like provisions of the Code.
Section 7. This ordinance shall become effective July 1, 1998.
Passed and Adopted on first reading this 11th day of May, 1998.

ORDINANCE NO. 260
AN ORDINANCE REGULATING LAND SUBDIVISIONS OF THE CITY OF ROSSVILLE, GEORGIA.
Footnote 1:
Editor's note— Appendix B contains the land subdivision regulations of the City of Rossville, Georgia, being Ord. No. 260, adopted Dec. 14, 1987. The provisions of said Ord. No. 260 have been included herein at the discretion of the editor and set out substantially as enacted. Amendatory legislation will be cited in parentheses following a particular amended section. Words contained in brackets have been included by the editor for clarity. For stylistic purposes, headings and catchlines have been made uniform and the same system of capitalization, citation to state statutes, and expression of numbers in text as appears in the Code of Ordinances has been used. Additions made for clarity are indicated by brackets.
Cross reference— Any ordinance dedicating or accepting any subdivision plat or adopting subdivision regulations saved from repeal, § 1-6(11); planning commission, § 2-161 et seq.; buildings and building regulations, ch. 22; environment, ch. 34; flood damage prevention, ch. 42; manufactured homes, ch. 46; signs, ch. 62; streets, sidewalks and other public places, ch. 70; zoning, app. A.
State Law reference— Approval by planning commission or governing authority on plat of subdivision required for filing or recording in superior court clerk's office, O.C.G.A. § 15-6-67(d); Georgia Land Sales Act, O.C.G.A. § 44-3-1 et seq.
1151: In pursuance of the authority conferred by Georgia General Planning and Zoning Enabling Act of 1957, as amended, the City Council of Rossville, Georgia, does ordain and enact into law the following articles and sections.
1153: This ordinance shall be known and may be cited as the "Land Subdivision Regulations of the City of Rossville, Georgia."
1155: No plat of a subdivision (as defined in Article III) within Rossville, Georgia shall be filed or recorded in the office of the clerk of the Superior Court of Walker County until it shall have been submitted to and approved by the planning commission and such approval entered in writing on the plat by the secretary of the planning commission.
1156: No land in the City of Rossville, Georgia shall hereafter be subdivided (as defined in Article III) and offered for sale, or sold or otherwise transferred in ownership by reference to or other use of a plat of a subdivision until said plat has received final approval by the planning commission, after which said plat shall then be duly recorded in the office of the clerk of the Superior Court of Walker County.
1157: Hereafter no building permit shall be issued for and no building or other structure shall be erected on any lot within the City of Rossville, Georgia unless the street giving access to the lot upon which said building is proposed to be placed shall be accepted or opened, as or shall have otherwise received the legal status of a public street prior to that time, or unless such street corresponds in its location and lines with a street shown on a subdivision plat approved by the planning commission or on a street located and accepted by the city council of Rossville.
1159:
31.1 The word "shall" is mandatory.
31.2 When not inconsistent with the context, words used in singular number include the plural and those used in the plural number include the singular.
31.3 Words used in the present tense include the future.
31.4 Planning commission shall mean Rossville planning commission.
31.5 City engineer shall mean city engineer of Rossville.
31.6 City council shall mean city council of Rossville.
31.7 City shall mean City of Rossville, Georgia.
31.8 Zoning ordinance shall refer to zoning ordinance of Rossville, Georgia.
31.9 Health department shall mean Walker County health department.
31.10 Clerk of superior court shall mean the clerk of the superior court of Walker County.
1160:
Except as specifically defined herein all words used in this ordinance have their customary dictionary definitions.
32.1 City specifications or standards: The specifications or standards of the City of Rossville, Georgia.
32.2 Lot: A portion or parcel of land separated from other portions or parcels by description as on a subdivision plat or record of survey map or as described by metes and bounds, and intended for transfer of ownership or for building development. For the purpose of this ordinance, the term does not include any portion of a dedicated right-of-way.
32.3 Major thoroughfare plan: The major thoroughfare plan that is part of Rossville's master plan for development.
32.4 Master plan: The comprehensive development plan of Rossville, Georgia including but not limited to: study of population and economy; land use and community facilities plans; major thoroughfare plan; zoning ordinance and subdivision regulations.
32.5 Plat: A map indicating the subdivision or resubdivision of land and intended to be filed for record.
32.6 Plat, final: A plat of a tract of land which meets the requirements of these regulations and is in form for recording in the office of the clerk of superior court of Walker County.
32.7 Plat, preliminary: A tentative proposal of a subdivision submitted to the planning commission for its consideration.
32.8 Street: A public way for vehicular traffic, whether designated as street, avenue, boulevard, road, highway, expressway, lane, alley, or other way. For the purpose of this ordinance "streets" are divided into the following categories:
32.81 Arterial, street: The streets so designated in the zoning ordinance of Rossville, Georgia.
32.82 Street collectors: The streets so designated in the zoning ordinance of Rossville, Georgia.
32.83 Minor street: The streets so designated in the zoning ordinance of Rossville, Georgia.
32.9 Subdivider: A person, firm or corporation having such a proprietary interest in the land to be subdivided as will authorize the maintenance of proceedings to subdivide such land under this ordinance, or the authorized agent of such person, firm or corporation for the purpose of proceeding under these regulations.
32.10 Subdivision: Division of a tract or parcel of land into two or more lots, building sites, or other divisions for the purpose, whether immediate or future, of sale, legacy or building development and includes all division of land involving a new street or change in existing streets, and includes resubdivision, and where appropriate to the context, relates to the process of subdividing or to the land or area subdivided, provided, however, that the following are not included within the definition:
1. The combination or recombination of portions of previously platted lots where the total number of lots is not increased and the resultant lots comply with the standards set forth in the zoning ordinance of the City of Rossville.
2. The division of land into parcels of five acres or more where no new street is involved.
3. The division of land into parcels where no new street is involved and the resultant lots comply with the standards set forth in the zoning ordinance of the City of Rossville.
1162: It is the intent of these regulations that the planning commission shall represent the city in all negotiations with the subdivider, and shall handle all negotiations between the city and the subdivider for such changes as may be necessary in the subdivision plats. Final approval of all subdivision plats shall be by the planning commission of Rossville.
1163: It shall be the duty of the secretary of the planning commission to give at least five days notice by registered or certified mail to the subdivision [subdivider] before the date on which the planning commission will review said subdivider's subdivision.
1164:
The subdivider shall prepare a preliminary plat, together with supplementary date as specified in article V, for purposes of conditional approval of preliminary plat.
Three copies of the preliminary plat and supplementary data specified and a filing fee of $1.00 per lot shall be submitted to the city clerk of Rossville, Georgia. The city clerk shall retain one copy and shall forward two copies and a copy of receipt for filing fee to the planning commission.
The planning commission shall, within 15 days, act on the preliminary plat giving consideration to (a) the conformity of the preliminary plat to these regulations, (b) the specific changes that may be required in the preliminary plat, and (c) the kind and extent of improvements to be made. The planning commission shall retain one copy and return one copy of the preliminary plat to the subdivider within the said 15 days, recording the note of conditional approval or disapproval on the plat. If approved, the planning commission shall state the conditions of such approval, if any, or if disapproved the commission shall state reasons therefor. Conditional approval shall be granted only in cases where no changes, or minor changes only, are required in the preliminary plat.
Conditional approval of a preliminary plat shall not constitute approval of the final plat. Rather, it shall be deemed an expression of approval of the layout submitted on the preliminary plat as a guide to the preparation of the final plat, which will be submitted for approval of the planning commission and for recording, upon fulfillment of the requirements of these regulations.
1165:
The subdivider, after notification by the planning commission with respect to the preliminary plat and the changes, if any, to be made therein, shall within six months thereafter file with the planning commission the final plat prepared as specified in article V. The final plat shall conform substantially to the preliminary plat as approved, and, if desired by the subdivider, it may constitute only that portion of the approved preliminary plat which he proposes to record and develop at the time, provided that such portion conforms to all requirements of these regulations.
Prior to the approval of the final plat the subdivider shall complete in accordance with the commission's decision, to the satisfaction of the planning commission, all the improvements required by the commission. Alternatively, he shall file with the planning commission a performance bond for the completion of improvements required by the planning commission, prior to the approval of the final plat.
One original and three copies of the final plat; supplementary data, as specified in article V; a filing fee of $1.00 per lot and a recording fee as prescribed by the city shall be submitted to the planning commission within six months after approval of the preliminary plat; otherwise, such approval shall become null and void unless an extension of time is granted by the planning commission.
Within 30 days after the submission of the final plat and supplementary data the planning commission shall afford a hearing to the subdivider sending by registered or certified mail the notice of time and place of hearing not less than five days before the date fixed therefor and shall express and note its final action on the plats and return the original and one copy to the subdivider. The planning commission shall retain one copy and file one copy with the city clerk, if disapproved, the reasons therefor shall be expressed on or attached to said plats.
1167:
The following plats and data are required as supplements to the procedures outlined under section 43, preapplication procedures:
51.1 General subdivision information. A description of existing conditions of the site and the proposed development, as necessary to supplement the drains required below. This information may include data on existing covenants, land characteristics and available community facilities and utilities; and information describing the subdivision proposal such as number of residential lots, typical lot width and depth, areas for business, play, recreation and other public uses and proposed street, utility and other improvements.
51.2 Location map. Showing the relationship of the proposed subdivision to the community; title, graphic scale, north arrow and date.
51.3 Sketch plan. The sketch plan may be a freehand sketch made directly on a print of a topographic survey, showing proposed layout of streets, lots and such other information found necessary by the planning commission.
1171:
All proposed subdivisions shall conform to the master plan of Rossville, Georgia. The densities established by the zoning ordinance of Rossville shall be observed by all subdividers.
61.1 Excavations. Any excavations or moving of earth shall conform to the specifications set forth in the Standard Excavation and Grading Code (1975 Edition) [see section 22-36 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Rossville] and to chapter [section] 34-126 et seq., and section 518-20 et seq. [sic] of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Rossville.
1172:
The arrangement, character, extent, location and grade of all streets shall be done in accordance with acceptable land planning principles and shall be considered in their relation to existing and planned streets, to topographical conditions, orientation, to public convenience and safety and in appropriate relation to the proposed uses of land to be served by such streets.
62.1 Access and circulation. Proposed streets shall be extended to the boundary lines of the tract to be subdivided and provide normal circulation of traffic within the subdivision.
62.2 Arrangement. The arrangement of streets in a subdivision shall either:
(a) Provide for the continuation or appropriate projection of existing principal streets in surrounding areas; or
(b) Conform to a plan for the neighborhood approved or adopted by the planning commission to meet a particular situation where topographical or other conditions make continuance or conformance to existing streets impracticable.
62.3 No through traffic on minor streets. Minor streets shall be so laid [out] that their use by through traffic in the subdivision will be discouraged.
62.4 Reserve strips. Unusual reserve strips controlling access to streets shall be prohibited. Land shall not be subdivided in a manner which omits part of the original tract to avoid drainage improvements.
62.5 Half streets. Half streets shall be prohibited.
62.6 Street jogs. Street jogs with centerline offsets of less than 150 feet shall not be permitted.
62.7 Reverse curves. A tangent at least 100 feet long shall be introduced between reverse curves on arterials and collectors.
62.8 Cul-de-sac. Streets designed to have one end permanently closed shall be provided at the closed end with a turnaround having a minimum right-of-way diameter of 80 feet.
62.9 Minimum right-of-way widths. In undeveloped or vacant areas the planning commission shall have the discretion of approving or classifying street types, such as arterials, collectors or minor streets. The right-of-way widths of street shall conform to the following minimum standards:
Street Type | Right-of-Way
Major arterial | 80;ft; minimum or greater subject to negotiation with the city
Minor arterial | 70;ft; minimum or greater subject to negotiation with the city
Major and minor collector | 60;ft; minimum or greater subject to negotiation with the city
Minor streets | 50;ft;
62.10 Pavement widths. The streets shall have the following minimum pavement widths unless otherwise recommended by the city engineer:
| Pavement Width
Street Type | Vertical Curb (feet) | Rolled Curb (feet)
Major arterial | 48 |
Minor arterial | 40 |
Major collector | 40 | 36
Minor collector | 40 | 36
Minor streets | 30 | 26
62.11 Grades. Street grades shall not exceed the following unless otherwise recommended and approved by the city engineer:
Street Type | Percent Grade
Major streets | 7
Collector streets | 10
Minor streets | 18
No street grade shall be less than 0.5%.
62.12 Visibility. When connecting street lines deflect from each other at any one point they shall be connected by a horizontal curve with a radius adequate to insure a sight distance of not less than 200 feet, measured along the centerline, for minor and collector streets and not less than 400 feet for major streets.
62.13 Intersections. Streets shall be laid out so as to intersect as nearly as possible at right angles and no street shall intersect any other street at less than 60 degrees. Intersections of minor streets with major arterials shall be held to a minimum.
Property lines at arterial and collector street intersections shall be rounded with a radius of 25 feet. An increased radius shall be required when the angle of intersection is less than 90 degrees.
Roadway and curb intersections shall be made concentric and shall be rounded by a radius of not less than 20 feet.
62.14 Street names. No new street names shall be used that will duplicate or be confused with the names of existing streets. Street names shall be subject to the approval of the planning commission.
(Ord. No. 283, § 1(a), (b), 1-8-90)
1173:
Alleys may be required in commercial and industrial districts, except that the planning commission may waive this requirement where other definite and assured provision is made for service access, such as off-street loading, unloading, and parking consistent with zoning requirements.
Alleys are not permitted in residential districts except when the planning commission determines that special conditions warrant a secondary means of access.
1174: Except where platting design makes it desirable, block lengths shall not exceed 1,200 feet or be less than 600 feet and shall normally be wide enough to allow two tiers of lots of appropriate depth.
1175:
The size, width, depth, shape, and the minimum setback lines shall be as indicated in the Rossville zoning ordinance.
65.1 Depth and width of properties reserved or laid out for commercial and industrial purposes shall be adequate to provide for the off-street service and parking facilities required by the type of use and development contemplated. Such properties shall have a minimum setback as indicated in the zoning ordinance.
65.2 Corner lots shall have minimum frontage and front and side yard setbacks as required by the zoning ordinance.
65.3 The subdividing of the land shall be such as to provide, by means of a public street, each lot with satisfactory access to an existing public street.
65.4 Double frontage and reverse frontage lots shall be avoided.
65.5 Side lot lines shall be substantially at right angles or radial to street lines.
1176:
Easements across lots or centered on rear or side lot lines shall be provided for utilities where necessary and shall be at least 16 feet in width.
Where a subdivision is traversed by a watercourse, drainage way, channel, or stream, there shall be provided a storm water easement or drainage right-of-way conforming substantially with the lines of such watercourse, and such further width or construction, or both, as will be adequate for the purpose. Parallel streets or parkways may be required by the planning commission in connection therewith.
1177:
67.1 When required by the planning commission, a drainage plan shall be made which shall take into account the ultimate development of the tributary area in which the proposed subdivision is located.
67.2 Low areas subject to periodic inundation shall not be developed or subdivided unless the commission determines that:
.21 The nature of the land use would not lend itself to damage by water to an appreciable extent; or that
.22 The area may be filled or improved in such a manner to prevent such periodic inundation; or that
.23 Minimum floor elevations may be established to prevent damage to buildings and structures.
67.3 The commission may require of the subdivider or his agent additional engineering information necessary to make decisions on acceptance of development in an area of questionable drainage. Such additional information shall be in writing and the certification of a qualified engineer may be required.
1178: Proposed subdivisions shall provide appropriate open spaces suitably located and of reasonable size for parks, playgrounds, play lots, or other recreational areas as may be necessary or practical. Such areas may consist of approximately five percent of the gross area of the proposed subdivision. The size and location of such parks and playgrounds are subject to the approval of the planning commission. In determining this requirement the planning commission shall give due consideration to the adequacy of existing parks and recreational facilities in the vicinity, size and characteristics of the subdivision and whether such requirement will result in exceptional hardship to the subdivider.
1180:
Iron pins shall be placed by the subdivider at all subdivision boundary lots and block corner angles points, points of curves in streets and at intermediate points as shall be required by the planning commission and shall meet the following specification:
71.1 Iron pins not less than 12 inches long and one-half inches in diameter set flush with the ground.
1181:
Each subdivider shall be required to install, at his own expense, or to have installed by the appropriate public agency, street and related improvements according to the following specifications:
72.1 All streets shall be cleared, grubbed and graded to the full right-of-way width. Finished grades shall be at levels approved by the planning commission.
72.2 Either rolled concrete curbs or integral concrete curb and gutter shall be installed on all streets. Adequate storm drainage pipes and catch basins, shall be installed where needed. Installation shall be according to sound engineering practices for proper drainage.
72.3 Curb breaks and driveways to property lines may be required by the planning commission according to standard engineering practices.
72.4 The planning commission may require sidewalks near commercial areas, schools and other places of public assembly and areas of intensive residential development such as apartment areas.
72.5 Streets shall be paved to the following widths:
Street Type | Pavement Width
Major or minor arterial | As approved or recommended by the planning commission
Major or minor—rolled curb | 36;ft;
Collector—vertical curb | 40;ft;
Minor street—rolled curb | 26;ft;
Minor street—vertical curb | 30;ft;
72.6 Street pavements shall be installed according to standard engineering practices, as outlined in the standard specifications for construction of roads and bridges of the Georgia D.O.T. (1977 Edition).
72.7 In certain cases as determined by the planning commission the subdivider may be required to pave a portion of a major street in order to insure proper access to the proposed subdivision.
72.8 Aluminum reflectorized street markers on plain pipes or posts of durable metal conforming to presently prevailing practices in the city, shall be furnished and set at all street intersections by the subdivider.
1182:
Except as herein provided, each lot or other site in a subdivision shall be connected to a public sanitary sewage system by lines of sufficient size to accommodate the anticipated sewage load. Lot service connections shall be stubbed in so that there will be no necessity for cutting into any pavement in order to make any future connection.
Three copies of the sewer plan, showing the seal of a registered professional engineer and showing the proposed sewer system in plan and profile as designed in accordance with sound engineering practices shall be submitted to be checked and approved by the planning commission prior to installation. The subdivider is responsible for installing approved sewer lines in a proper manner.
Wherever a sanitary sewage system is not available within a reasonable distance, septic tanks may be permitted upon obtaining special permission of the Walker County health department. For septic tank installations the minimum lot size shall be 20,000 square feet with 100 feet of frontage or greater if so required by the health department. The following information shall be submitted to the health department for consideration of septic tank approval:
73.1 Topographic information for each parcel of land on which a septic tank is to be installed, contour interval shall not exceed five feet.
73.2 Location of all drainage facilities either natural or proposed.
Percolation data indicated on a plat as specified by the health department.
1183:
Each lot or other site in a subdivision shall be connected to a public water supply system by lines of sufficient size to accommodate the anticipated water demand. Lot service connections shall be stubbed in so that there will be no necessity for cutting into any pavement in order to make any future connections.
Three copies of the plan of the water supply system of the subdivision, showing the seal of a registered professional engineer, shall be submitted to, checked and approved by the planning commission prior to installation. Said system shall be designed in accordance with standard engineering practice.
Arrangements for the installation of the water system are the responsibility of the subdivider.
1184:
Fire hydrants shall be installed by the subdivider according to the city standards.
Cross reference— Fire prevention and protection, ch. 38.
1185: All underground work such as sewers, water lines, gas mains and telephone conduits shall be installed and earth backfill compacted before street pavement is laid.
1187: The paving requirements of this ordinance may be waived on request of the subdivider for a subdivision of four lots or less which involves either the extension of an unpaved street or the opening of a new street, provided that such street extension or new street shall not exceed 400 feet in length, and shall end in a permanent dead-end or intersect another street. All land which abuts upon such street extension or new street shall be within the subdivision for which the waiver of paving is granted and shall not be subject to further subdividing.
1188: The street right-of-way requirements of this ordinance may be reduced on the request of the subdivider for a subdivision of four lots or less which involves the extension of an existing street with a right-of-way width smaller than that required by this ordinance or which involves the opening of a new street. Provided, however, that such street extension or new street shall not exceed 400 feet in length and shall end in a permanent dead-end or intersect another street. All land which abuts upon such street extension or new street shall be within the subdivision for which the modifications of the right-of-way is granted and shall not be subject to further subdividing. In no case shall a right-of-way be reduced to less than 40 feet.
1189: When a peculiar shape, or the topography of a tract of land, or other unusual condition, makes it impractical for a developer to comply with the literal interpretations of the design requirements of this ordinance, the planning commission shall be authorized to vary such requirements, provided, however, that in so doing the intents and purposes of this ordinance are not violated.
1190: In granting modifications, the planning commission may require such conditions as will, in its judgement, secure substantially the objectives of the standards or requirements so modified.
1191:
The planning commission may waive, vary, or modify the standards and requirements of these regulations if, in its judgement, an unusual or experimental subdivision might have merits because of:
85.1 Judicious use of unusual materials in constructing required improvements.
85.2 Use of new design concepts such as cluster subdivisions.
1192: Where necessary, in the opinion of the planning commission, to carry out the provisions of this ordinance, the planning commission is authorized to hire a licensed civil engineer, for the purposes of consultation or inspection. There is hereby appropriated the sum of $1,000.00 for such purpose.
1194: Whenever these subdivision regulations impose more restrictive standards than other applicable local ordinances the requirements of these regulations shall govern. Whenever the provisions of any applicable local ordinances require more restrictive standards than are required by these regulations, the provisions of such ordinances shall govern.
1195: All ordinances or regulations and part of ordinances or regulations in conflict herewith are repealed.
1196: The owner or agent of the owner of any land to be subdivided within the city, who transfers or sells such land by reference to or exhibition of or by other use of a plat of subdivision of such land before the plat has been approved by the planning commission and recorded in the office of the clerk of the superior court of Walker County, shall be guilty of misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as provided by law. The description by metes and bounds in the instrument of transfer or other document used in the process of selling or transfer shall not exempt the transaction from such penalties. The city may enjoin such transfer or sale or agreement by appropriate action.
1197: Should any section or provision of these subdivision regulations be declared by the courts to be unconstitutional or invalid, such declaration shall not affect any other portion or provision of these subdivision regulations.
1198: These subdivision regulations shall take effect and be in force from and after their adoption, the public welfare demanding it.
1199:
The provisions of this ordinance shall be included and incorporated in the Code of Ordinances of the City of Rossville, Georgia, as an addition or amendment thereto and shall be appropriately renumbered to conform to the uniform numbering system of the Code.
